title: huami1314/GestaltX
author: huami1314
body:
GestaltX

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.6-blue)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-27.x-black?logo=apple)](#compatibility) [![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-SwiftUI-orange?logo=swift)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv3-blue)](LICENSE) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_ZH-CN.md) · [日本語](README_JA.md) · [한국어](README_KO.md) · [Türkçe](README_TR.md) A MobileGestalt editor for iPhone and iPad. Developed by [huamidev](https://github.com/huamidev). ## Features | Category | Presets and tools | | --- | --- | | Display | Dynamic Island capability and layout, Always-On Display, AOD Vibrancy, high-luminance AOD, AOD flipbook, HDR photo display, wallpaper parallax, Liquid Glass low-power rendering, experimental PWM and DisplayPort flags | | Device | Model name, boot/shutdown chime, charge limit, tap to wake, Camera Control settings, Action Button settings, Collision SOS, Audio Mix, Spatial FaceTime audio | | iPad | Apple Pencil settings, Stage Manager capability, iPad app compatibility | | Intelligence | Independent region-code options, Apple Intelligence capability flag, on-device Siri, Audio Intelligence, Personal Translator, Photos Clean Up, Handwriting Synthesis, always-listening Hey Siri, and sales-region options for activation attempts on China-mainland devices | | Advanced | Apple internal feature flags, the system-wide InternalBuild flag with explicit enable confirmation, internal settings bundle, Security Research Device flag | | Field editor | Read, search, add, edit, and remove `CacheExtra` fields; local plist import/export; String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Data, Date, Array, and Dictionary values | | Changes | Automatic reading and manual re-read, staged before/after review, verified writes, per-preset restore | | Backups | Automatic initial backup before device editing, backup before every write, original-value records; open, export, restore, and delete | | Logs & respring | Actual exploit-stage logs and manual NeoSpring respring | Usually, changing the region code is enough to try enabling AI; there is no need to change Sales Region. Selecting United States for Region Code sets `RegionCode` to `LL` and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code. *If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.* Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added. Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. China-mainland devices can use the Apple Intelligence and region options to attempt activation; availability also depends on the model, OS version, and Apple services. ### Apple Intelligence, Face ID and dictation The [YumEdit 1.2.1 approach](https://github.com/H4CNPE/YumEdit/tree/v1.2.1) avoids spoofing the product, board and CPU. In Intelligence, **Apple Intelligence Capability** sets the generative-model flag to `1`, while the separate **Siri AI Mode** preset sets `SiriMode` to `2`. Neither changes hardware identity nor the device-specific On-Device Siri capability. These are experimental flags, not a guarantee of resource downloads or working Apple Intelligence. YumEdit later replaced this activation approach with an experimental two-stage workflow; GestaltX does not implement temporary hardware spoofing. If a previous hardware spoof broke Face ID or dictation, choose an original device backup in **Backups → Restore Hardware Identity**. Alternatively, import a verified original plist and use **Intelligence → Restore Hardware Identity**. Save or discard pending changes first. Recovery requires a verified same-device backup with the same `CacheData`, `CacheUUID` and cache version, whose product and board match the kernel-reported hardware. It restores only product, board, CPU and the original regulatory model number, preserving current AI, Siri, region and unrelated settings. Unlike YumEdit's region activation, recovery does not substitute a US regulatory model. Missing, incompatible or already-spoofed backups are rejected; original hardware values are never guessed. Recovery currently recognizes iPhone 11 through iPhone 15/15 Plus (including the second- and third-generation SE), checking the original CPU against the known chip for the physical product. Other products are rejected rather than guessing their chip. A backup is created before writing and the complete result is verified. **Fully restart the device, then test Face ID, dictation and Apple Intelligence.** This recovery addresses hardware-spoofing damage, not every possible Face ID fault; device-level behavior still requires testing on affected hardware. ## Compatibility Supports **iOS / iPadOS 27.x**. **iOS / iPadOS 26.x is not supported for on-device MobileGestalt access.** Powered by [worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query). SystemGroup access requires iOS 27; available features depend on the device and OS. Local plist editing is also supported. Signing requires a certificate and provisioning profile with at least one usable App Group. Sign the app and its embedded share extension with at least one **common App Group**, and keep the extension when re-signing. Both processes detect their actual signed App Groups at runtime. Distributed IPAs carry ad-hoc signatures with these entitlements embedded so SideStore and AltStore can detect them when re-signing; they are not signed with a developer certificate. ## Download Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX/releases/latest). Some users report incomplete downloads with Safari on iOS 27. If the file is reported as damaged or cannot be extracted, download it again; several attempts may be needed. Try another browser if it persists. The cause has not been confirmed. ## Import a plist In Files or another app, select a MobileGestalt plist, tap **Share**, and choose **GestaltX**. The share extension reads the supplied file and hands it to the app through the shared App Group. Return to GestaltX if it does not open automatically. The app checks a device-bound proof from a GestaltX export, or at least two unique identifiers obtained from this device, then asks you to confirm the import. Files that cannot be verified are rejected. Previously imported files are never used as the reference for device identity. Some original plists contain no unique device identifiers. Export a copy from GestaltX on this device first: its verification key stays in the device-only Keychain and is never included in the file. Shared files are checked at launch and on return to the foreground. Pending edits are preserved until you save or discard them. Confirmed imports open as local documents. **MG Control** supports adding, editing, renaming and deleting typed keys and values. Use **Restore Imported Plist** to restore a verified file to this device; restoration requires a matching system cache layout and an additional confirmation, backs up the current file, and verifies the write. Restart the device afterward. ## Language support GestaltX follows your iOS language settings, with English as the default and fallback. Persian includes right-to-left layout support. | Language | Locale | | --- | --- | | English | `en` | | 简体中文 — Simplified Chinese | `zh-Hans` | | 繁體中文（台灣）— Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) | `zh-Hant-TW` | | 繁體中文（香港）— Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong) | `zh-Hant-HK` | | Tiếng Việt — Vietnamese | `vi` | | Русский — Russian | `ru` | | فارسی — Persian | `fa` | | 한국어 — Korean | `ko` | | Español — Spanish | `es` | | 日本語 — Japanese | `ja` | | Türkçe — Turkish | `tr` | ## Credits - [forcequitOS / Taj C — worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query) - [neonmodder123](https://github.com/neonmodder123) - [skadz108](https://github.com/skadz108) - [rooootdev — NeoSpring](https://github.com/rooootdev/neospring) - [Nouvborne — Ketamine](https://github.com/Nouvborne/Ketamine) - [PoomSmart — MGKeys](https://github.com/PoomSmart/MGKeys) - [leminlimez — Nugget](https://github.com/leminlimez/Nugget) - [rooootdev — mond](https://github.com/rooootdev/mond) - [frs0n — GestaltEdit](https://github.com/frs0n/GestaltEdit) ## Disclaimer For security research and educational purposes only. Use only on devices you own or are authorized to manage. Back up your data before making changes. Modifying MobileGestalt may cause system instability or require a device restore. You are responsible for the changes you apply and the resulting risks. ## License [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE) · Copyright © 2026 huamidev. ## Star History

title: erkamyaman/rust-anything
author: erkamyaman
body:
rust-anything

English · Türkçe · Українська · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Deutsch · Français · Русский · 日本語 · 한국어 · Azərbaycanca · Oʻzbekcha · Қазақша · Кыргызча · Türkmençe · Татарча · ئۇيغۇرچە · Português · Tiếng Việt

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.
Point it at your app: it records what the original does, your coding agent writes the Rust one piece at a time,
and every piece is checked against that recording before it moves on. It doesn't translate code; it proves the rewrite.


Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · MCP Registry · Real-world ports · FAQ
Languages · How it works · Whole apps · Sponsors · MIT
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by CodeRabbit

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical


Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: record, replay and the front door today; unit ports come next.

Record
record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws. 		Port
bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust. 		Check
diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes. 		Lift
When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on [napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Whole tools and servers, or only the slow part, one hot path at a time: | Real project, same output as the original | Original | With rust-anything | | --- | ---: | ---: | | [Prettier](docs/real-world.md#prettier) 3.6.2, 2,360 JS/TS files from the command line | 128.6 s | **6.9 s: 19x faster** | | Prettier, 6,305 Markdown files from the command line | 352 s | **22.5 s: 15.6x faster** | | [json-server](docs/real-world.md#json-server), a whole Node server: memory at idle | 74 MB | **3.5 MB**, one 5.3 MB binary | | json-server, from start to first response | 79 to 85 ms | **8 to 10 ms** | | [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) search over 50,000 strings, per query | 91.2 ms | **2.8 ms: 32x faster** | Prettier: 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs format fully in Rust across 10 languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, JSON, GraphQL, YAML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, Less), and all 17,224 match Prettier byte for byte, since anything not ported yet falls back to Prettier. json-server: 514/514 recorded HTTP cases match on a pure Rust binary. Measured on an Apple M4, two runs each, every output compared before timing ([details](docs/real-world.md)). Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. Against C the win is safety, not speed: [ffmpeg's libavutil](docs/real-world.md#ffmpeg) ported to Rust matches all 226,447 recorded calls and runs at about C's speed (18 of 42 benchmarks even, 8 faster, 16 slower by 3 to 40%).


json-server, a whole Node server, lifted to a pure Rust binary (Apple M4). How it was measured.

> rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project > or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation. > [!WARNING] > `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on > many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay` > run the same cases again, on the port or the original. Code that writes files, talks to a > database or calls the network does that once per case. Run them on a copy of the project, with a > test database and no production credentials in the environment. ## Quick start Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or OpenCode and let your agent install it: ```text Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`. Tell me when to restart you. ``` Or yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # from crates.io rust-anything setup # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode ``` No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary. In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above must be on your `PATH`): ```text /plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything ``` `setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it. Then ask your agent, for example: - *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."* - *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."* - *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."* - *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."* ### Works with | Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds | | --- | --- | | Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` | | Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` | | Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | OpenCode | MCP server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`mcp.servers`), skill in `~/.config/opencode/skills/` | | Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](docs/install.md#install)) | Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`); `--no-backup` skips the copy. To wire OpenCode up by hand, put the server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`command` is the whole argv) and copy [`skills/rust-anything/`](./skills/rust-anything) to `~/.config/opencode/skills/rust-anything/`: ```json { "mcp": { "servers": { "rust-anything": { "type": "local", "command": ["rust-anything", "mcp"] } } } } ``` Or run the steps yourself: ```sh rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs # what is hot, and who calls it rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text # write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then: rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs # every recorded case must match rust-anything fuzz rust/fuzzy-rs --time 60 --keep # fresh inputs: what the recording missed rust-anything bench rust/fuzzy-rs # faster? the verdict says rust-anything gate rust/fuzzy-rs # done means this passes ``` rust-anything does not translate code: your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, ...) or you write the Rust. rust-anything supplies what an agent cannot guess reliably: where the time goes, what to port first and in which order, a bridge so the rest of the code calls the Rust with its API unchanged, the exact behavior the port must match, a safe way to ship it, and a gate that says when a port is done. Same output is not enough. Record what the app sends too, and a rewrite that mails twice fails:


A real run of app record --effects and app replay. See Side effects.

## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | Kotlin | Gradle module of top-level functions and `@JvmStatic` methods | the Java bridge: typed JNI in Java wrapper classes calling the compiled Kotlin statics | a generated reflection driver, with the Kotlin sources compiled by `kotlinc` | | PHP | folder of functions and `public static` methods | coming next: PHP FFI over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | C# | folder of `public static` methods | coming next: P/Invoke over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); a Gradle module with `.kt` sources and no `.java` sources is Kotlin, mixed modules stay Java. `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java, Kotlin and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. For Android, `rust-anything build --profile android` builds the same JNI library with the NDK for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a` and `x86_64` (or the `--abi` values you pass) and installs it into `/jniLibs//`; `--api` sets the API level (minimum 26, which the generated Java runtime needs). It finds the NDK from `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`/`ANDROID_NDK_ROOT` or the SDK, needs the Rust targets (`rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi x86_64-linux-android`), links 64-bit libraries with 16 KB page alignment, and checks that every JNI entry point is exported. Gradle looks in `src/main/jniLibs` by default, so pass `--jni-libs app/src/main/jniLibs` or add `/jniLibs` to `sourceSets.main.jniLibs.srcDirs`. `rust-anything record --profile android` runs the original Kotlin unit under ART on a connected device (adb), dexes the generated driver with `d8` from the SDK's build-tools, and pulls the results back as the same `cases.jsonl`; `diff --profile android` replays them against the `.so` built for the device's ABI. Both need `adb`, a device, `kotlinc`, an SDK with build-tools and a platform, and `--device ` when more than one device is connected. The profile covers logic units: Activity/Compose/XML UI, lifecycle and SDK-only classes stay in Kotlin, and each call crosses JNI, so prefer the generated batch wrappers for hot loops. On a host, `record` and `diff` keep using the desktop JVM. For PHP, `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. Porting its units into Rust through PHP's FFI is the next step ([issue #2](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/2)). C# works the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door; porting units through P/Invoke comes next. ## Learn more - [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): the loop, what `bridge` and `analyze` decide, hot paths, what it can't catch, what a real port takes, and keeping up with the original (`map`) - [Ship a port as a package](docs/packaging.md): maturin wheels and napi-rs per-platform npm packages, with the CI that builds them - [Port a whole app](docs/whole-apps.md): servers, CLIs and libraries, from the front door to `app lift` - [Examples and case studies](docs/examples.md): x18n, and real code in six languages - [Real-world ports](docs/real-world.md): json-server, Fuse.js, vercel/ms, with benchmarks - [Install, update and develop](docs/install.md): every install method, Windows, and building from source - [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Status](docs/STATUS.md) · [MCP tools](docs/tools.md) ## Sponsors

rust-anything is free and open source. If it helps your work, please consider sponsoring it.
Your support keeps development going.

## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome; [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) covers the setup, where tests go, and how to add a language. Design choices and their reasons are in [DECISIONS.md](./DECISIONS.md). Case studies of real ports are especially welcome. Please report security problems privately ([SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md)), and see the [code of conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © [Erkam Yaman](https://github.com/erkamyaman). Ports and generated code in your repository are yours.

# BatteryHub *Formerly **Wireless Battery**. Version 1.1.0 renamed the app; an update keeps your settings, startup choice and battery history.* [![Support me on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ko--fi-Support%20me-FF5E5B?logo=ko-fi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/krisgfx) [![Donate with PayPal](https://img.shields.io/badge/PayPal-Donate-00457C?logo=paypal&logoColor=white)](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/krisgfx) [![GitHub Sponsors](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Sponsor-EA4AAA?logo=githubsponsors&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sponsors/krisgfx9) [![Join our Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20us-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/ZgDDUPP8ye) [![Star on GitHub](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor?style=flat&logo=github&label=Star)](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor) [![Share on Reddit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Reddit-Share-FF4500?logo=reddit&logoColor=white)](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fkrisgfx9%2FWireless-Device-Battery-Monitor&title=Wireless%20Battery%3A%20battery%20levels%20of%20your%20wireless%20devices%20on%20the%20Windows%20taskbar) [![Report a device](https://img.shields.io/badge/Report-a%20device-2EA44F?logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/issues/new) [![Help translate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Help-translate-6F42C1?logo=googletranslate&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/pull/129) Battery levels of your wireless mouse, headset, keyboard and controller, right on the Windows taskbar. ![BatteryHub on the taskbar](docs/screenshot.png) > **Just want it working?** Download **[BatteryHub-Setup](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest)** from the latest release. Use the per-user installation for setup without administrator rights; see the [installation notes](#install) for unsigned-app warnings and the all-users option. > > **Experienced users** can grab the portable zip, use the [command-line options](#command-line), or [build it from source](#build) with `make` or `build.bat`. > > **Like it?** BatteryHub is free and open source. If it saves you a trip into vendor software, you can support it on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/krisgfx), [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/krisgfx) or [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/krisgfx9). It helps me keep my apps free alongside my studies. Not able to donate? A ⭐ star, sharing it, or reporting an unsupported device with a `--dump` helps just as much. - **Tiny**: a ~350 KB app using about 2 MB of RAM. It's plain C++/Win32, with no runtime and no background service, and supports per-user installation without administrator rights. - **Vendor apps usually aren't required**: most drivers query devices directly. Some headsets use the bundled [HeadsetControl](https://github.com/Sapd/HeadsetControl) helper. Device-specific setup, firmware patches and conflicts with vendor apps are described in the table and [Limitations](#limitations). - **Many brands**: Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Glorious, Jabra, JBL, PlayStation and Xbox controllers, Samsung Galaxy Buds, any Bluetooth device Windows knows a battery level for, and every headset the bundled [HeadsetControl](https://github.com/Sapd/HeadsetControl) supports. ## Display **On the taskbar (default):** `🎧 30% 🖱 93%` next to the notification area, drawn with the Windows icon font. - **Low battery:** a red number means 15% or less. - **Charging:** a blue ⚡ appears next to the number. Once the device is fully charged and still on power, it turns into a green ✓. - **Asleep:** dimmed text means the device is asleep and the last known value is shown. Turn off *Dim sleeping devices* in the menu to keep that value at full brightness. - **Disconnected (optional):** turn on *Show disconnected devices* to display a dimmed `×` for devices whose driver explicitly reports an offline wireless link. This does not infer disconnection from a missed battery poll; the default remains to hide offline devices. - **Two devices of one kind:** with two mice (or two controllers...) both would get the same icon, so each one gets a tiny caption of up to 3 letters in the corner of its icon, taken from its name (`MX`, `PRO`), or a number when the names do not tell them apart. A device that is alone in its kind shows no caption. - **Theme:** it follows light/dark mode and DPI scaling. - **Transparent taskbar themes** (e.g. Windhawk's Taskbar Styler): turn on *Background behind taskbar text* in the menu to keep the text readable over the wallpaper. - **Several monitors:** the widget shows on every monitor's taskbar, next to its clock, so it stays visible while a game runs fullscreen. *Show the widget on* in the menu picks *All monitors*, *Main monitor only*, or one display (e.g. only *Display 3*). - **More display options:** *Icons above percentages* stacks each icon over its level to save width; *Brand colors* shows known brands in their color (Razer green, HyperX red, ...) with a small level bar; two devices of the same kind get a tiny caption so they can be told apart; left and right taskbars get a column of devices. - **Languages:** English, العربية, Deutsch, Español, فارسی, Français, עברית, 日本語, 한국어, Magyar, Polski, Português (Brasil), Русский, Svenska, Tiếng Việt, Türkçe, Українська, 简体中文 and 繁體中文. The app follows the Windows display language; *Language* in the menu picks another one. The name is shown in the taskbar widget's tooltip/caption, tray tooltip and notifications, and the device menu. Use *Reset to original name* to restore the driver's name. Renaming never changes driver matching, protocol queries, or `--list` / `--dump` diagnostic output. No account or network access is needed. Hover for details. Click for the menu: every device (click one to hide or show it), display mode, *Refresh now*, *Start with Windows*, and *Exit*. Levels refresh every 60 seconds (*Check battery every* in the menu changes this), and right away when a device is plugged in or the PC wakes up. ## Smart Battery Alerts (experimental) You can set a **per-device low-battery notification threshold** from each device's submenu: **Battery alerts** → *Use default (15%)*, *Disable notifications*, or one of 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%. The existing 15% default stays unchanged unless you choose an override. Settings are stored by device key in the current user's Windows registry (`Software\WirelessBattery`, `AlertThresholds`). An alert is triggered only from a real, fresh 0–100% battery reading when the device is connected, awake and not charging. An alert is issued once, and will re-arm after the level climbs more than 10 percentage points above the chosen threshold (or when charging begins). Missing readings or sleeping devices do not retrigger alerts. Hidden devices don't produce notifications. Disabling notifications for one device does not hide it or change its percentage. Both taskbar-widget and tray-icon modes support notifications. Since Windows needs a notification-area icon to display a legacy balloon, widget mode may show a temporary notification icon for up to one minute after an alert. Widget colours and the low-battery highlight still use the project's original global 15% threshold, independently of the notification setting. ## Battery history & insights Right-click a device in the taskbar widget or tray menu and choose **Battery history...**. The native, DPI-aware viewer (it follows the Windows light/dark theme) shows recorded battery levels with connected sample lines over the last **24 hours**, **7 days**, or **30 days**, along with the latest reading, lowest/highest level, change in percentage points, and sample count. You can clear the selected device's history from the viewer. History is recorded **locally only** for connected, awake devices reporting a numeric percentage. Readings are sampled at most once every 30 minutes per device (except charging-state transitions, with a 60-second minimum). Data is kept for up to 30 days and the local file is kept under about 2 MB. The app never probes hardware beyond its existing polling, sends no history data over the network, and makes a conservative, approximate time-to-empty estimate from recent discharge observations only. At least four points, two hours, a three-percentage-point decline, a fresh reading and a stable discharge segment are required. Charging, old readings or insufficient data suppress the estimate; device-reported runtime is not available. The estimate is not a guarantee. Missing chart data is shown as gaps, not interpolated. Turn off **Record battery history** in the menu to stop saving readings; what was already saved stays until you clear it in the viewer. The file is stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\WirelessBattery\battery_history.tsv`. Its device identities are encoded (not encrypted); the file is local to your Windows account. In `--demo`, the chart uses synthetic data that is never saved. **Note:** history starts collecting only after this feature is installed and the app has been running for a while. ## Supported devices Match your model, receiver VID:PID, connection mode and any firmware requirements to the table; `BatteryHub.exe --dump` shows the IDs. Drawing tablets are skipped automatically. ## Updates on Windows Official stable Windows builds check the project's latest published stable release in the background, 30 seconds after startup and then every 24 hours while the app is running. Open the menu to see **Update available: vX.Y.Z...**, or choose **Check for updates...** yourself. Update information appears only in this menu: battery icons, percentages and tooltips stay the same, and automatic checks never show a notification or dialog. Turn off **Automatically check for updates** in the menu to disable background checks. For an installed copy, click the update entry and **Download and install**. Nothing is installed without that click. The app downloads the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` and its signature, checks the signature against the maintainer's public key built into the app, downloads the Windows installer, and runs it only if its SHA-256 is the one in the signed list (and the one GitHub lists for it). It then updates the existing installation. Settings and startup preference are preserved, and the app reopens after installation. An installation for all users can ask for administrator permission. **Release notes** opens the official release page; **Later** keeps your current version. Portable copies offer the release page for downloading the ZIP manually. Checks contact GitHub's public API without an account or token. No device or battery information is sent. Offline failures and GitHub rate limits leave battery monitoring running; a previously found release stays in the menu until a successful check supersedes it or it is installed. Cancelling a download waits for the current network operation to finish its finite timeout. The installer never restarts Windows automatically. **Why updates are safe to install:** the signing key never goes to GitHub. The maintainer signs each release's checksum list on their own PC (see [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md)), so even someone who took over the GitHub account or its build workflow could not publish an update the app would install. A release without a valid signature is shown in the menu but can only be downloaded by hand. The signature does not replace Windows' own SmartScreen or UAC prompts. Install the first release containing this feature manually once. Development/test builds disable official update checks so local changes cannot be replaced accidentally. Updates for Linux and automatic replacement of portable copies are deferred. ## Command line ``` BatteryHub.exe --list # print every device and its battery level, then exit BatteryHub.exe --json # print a JSON array of devices and battery levels, then exit BatteryHub.exe --dump # every HID collection, HID devices that could not be opened, all USB devices (also ones # without a HID interface) and Bluetooth devices; also saved to %TEMP%\BatteryHub-dump.txt BatteryHub.exe --report # open the "Request support for a device" window BatteryHub.exe --demo # sample devices of every brand instead of real ones (screenshots, checking colors) BatteryHub.exe --quit # close the running instance ``` The Linux build uses the same flags with `wireless-battery` instead of `BatteryHub.exe`, and also accepts `--help`. `--json` prints a stable array that scripts and bar widgets can parse: ```json [{"key":"kysona:373B:1085","name":"CX Wireless mouse","via":"2.4 GHz receiver","kind":"mouse", "percent":85,"level":"","detail":"","charging":false,"asleep":false,"connected":true, "millivolts":4029,"graceSec":1800}] ``` `graceSec` is how long the app keeps showing the last known level while the device is asleep. Adding new fields is backwards compatible. **Device not shown?** Right-click the widget or tray icon and choose **Request support for a device...**. Pick the device, check what will be sent (it is shown word for word: the device name, its type, its USB/HID ids and interface layout, and your optional name and notes) and click **Send**. It goes on the public list at [krisgfx.com/tools](https://krisgfx.com/tools/#requested) and opens or updates a GitHub issue. **Copy full report** puts the complete `--dump` on the clipboard for the issue. Report data is sent only when you click Send. Official Windows builds can also contact GitHub to check for updates, as described in [Updates on Windows](#updates-on-windows); update checks do not send device or battery information. ## Build You need [MinGW-w64](https://www.mingw-w64.org/), e.g. from [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/) (`pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc make`). ``` make # development build, version 0.0.0 build.bat # plain cmd with g++ and windres on PATH make VERSION=1.2.3 CHANNEL=test # versioned build, official updates disabled build.bat 1.2.3 test # equivalent versioned cmd build make test VERSION=1.2.3 CHANNEL=test # device and updater regression tests ``` To build the installer and portable zip, install [Inno Setup](https://jrsoftware.org/isinfo.php), first build with the intended version (for example `make VERSION=1.2.3 CHANNEL=test`), then run `powershell -File installer\build-installer.ps1 -Version 1.2.3`. Packaging rejects a version that differs from the executable. It downloads the pinned HeadsetControl release and verifies its checksum. GitHub Actions does all of this automatically: pushing a tag like `v1.0.0` publishes a release with the installer, the portable zip and the HeadsetControl source (as its GPL license requires). Windows builds also need PowerShell for generating the shared executable/resource version. The official repository's version tags build with `CHANNEL=stable`; local builds default to `dev`. Forks and pull requests do not enable official updates automatically. `BatteryHub.exe` on its own also works. Without `headsetcontrol.exe` next to it (or on `PATH`) you just lose the extra headsets. ## Linux (experimental) A Linux build sits alongside the Windows app. It uses the same vendor drivers with a hidraw-based HID backend and a GTK4 StatusNotifierItem tray icon; the Windows code path is unchanged. On Windows 10 the task-button area is narrowed automatically. - **Phones:** read from a file Phone Link writes for the Start menu companion card, which is not a documented API and may change with Phone Link updates. The phone shows while Phone Link reports it as connected; a card older than 3 hours is shown dimmed. The card also says when the phone is charging, which shows as the charging bolt. - **Sleeping devices:** a device that is asleep may not answer. Its last value stays visible, dimmed unless *Dim sleeping devices* is turned off in the menu. Logitech receivers drop sleeping devices from the link, so their last value is kept for 30 minutes. - **HECATE G2 Wireless 7.1 headset** (2.4 GHz dongle `35BB:A009` / `A209`): no battery query for its dongle is documented yet, so it is not read. Keychron mice are supported. - **Baseus AeQur GH02 headset:** the 2.4 GHz dongle (`10D6:4802`, Actions chip) only carries audio, media keys and the chip's firmware-update channel, not the battery. Connect the headset over Bluetooth to see its level (shown via the Bluetooth support when Windows reports one). - **Weikav Lucky65 v1 keyboard:** the firmware does not report its battery over the 2.4 GHz dongle (`0603:0351`, Novatek chip). Apex 5 was tested on real hardware over the 2.4 GHz receiver and a USB cable; Vader 5 Pro follows SDL and Windows hardware traces. - **Not supported yet:** MSI devices outside the models listed in the table, Razer Kraken headsets, Barracuda models other than the Barracuda X (2022) (`1532:0550` / `0552`) and Barracuda Pro (`1532:053A`), HyperX Pulsefire mice other than the Haste 2 Wireless / Haste 2 Core Wireless / Haste 2 Mini, and the Xbox Wireless Headset on the Xbox adapter are not covered by the current drivers. body:
s2arm.com

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [English](README.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md)

> [!NOTE] > **[s2arm.com](https://s2arm.com) is the official S2Arm website.** S2Arm is free and open source and never accepts donations; get S2Arm only from [s2arm.com](https://s2arm.com) or this GitHub repository. **Your own Switch games, running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac.** Game code is rewritten to native ARM64 and runs directly on the device's processor, with graphics going straight to Metal. From 0.6.0 there is a single S2Arm app on your phone and every game lives in its library: in the Mac or Windows launcher, send games to your iPhone one by one and play. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS / iPadOS 18 and later) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later) · Mac or Windows launcher · License: Apache-2.0 · **Bring your own games** [Download the launcher](https://s2arm.com) · [All releases](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/releases) · [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md)

## What's new in 0.6.0 ### One app for all your games Install S2Arm on your phone once, then add games one by one. Updating or renewing S2Arm never means installing your games again, and your saves stay. Sign with a free or paid Apple ID or a developer certificate, or sign it yourself and import it. ### Snapshots: save this moment, come back any time No need to wait for the game's own save point. In a game, tap the ◉ in the top-right corner to save the moment you're in; press and hold it and choose Go back to the saved moment to return. Next time, Continue from this moment at the top of the library takes you straight there. - Each game keeps only the latest snapshot; a new one replaces the old. - A snapshot takes storage on your phone (the size depends on the game). Press and hold to delete it and free the space, or turn snapshots off in Settings. - A snapshot only works on the device that saved it, and still works after you update S2Arm.

### One file, any of your devices Export any game as a .s2arm file and import it on another of your devices to play; the phone signs it by itself. Each game keeps one copy of its files, and Free up space shows what games, saves and snapshots take. ### Every shader, ready from the first play Shaders the game needs are prepared when you send it, so new areas no longer stutter the first time. Player diagnostics collected **26,809** shaders from 69 games that failed to compile on the device. Leaving out 278 damaged inputs that can't be read as shaders, **all 26,531** of the rest now compile. How it is counted: the rate covers only shaders that **had failed to compile** in player diagnostics; it is not a coverage rate for all shaders. Of the remaining 98, 91 were not shaders at all but memory read wrongly during capture (capture fixed), and the other 7 have been fixed at the root. Note: on iPhone, precompiled pipelines are generated only when you Push to iPhone with that iPhone connected. When exporting for self-signing (no iPhone connected) or with several iPhones connected, this version still compiles them the first time they are needed, as in 0.5. This will improve in a later version. ### Fixes, performance and graphics From 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 (how each number is counted is in the table): | | Number | How it's counted | |---|---|---| | Fixes merged | **344** | Fix commits merged into main after 0.5.0 | | Player reports handled | **156** | Feedback issues closed after 0.5.0 | | Community contributions | **126** | Pull requests from players and developers | | GPU render time | **−50%** | Deferred-lighting scene, 4.8–5.9 ms → 2.7 ms | | Build memory peak | **−35%** | Peak memory while building large games | Also: several kinds of shader problems fixed at the root, more reliable loading and saving, smoother frame generation, and steadier app install, signing and sending on Windows and Mac. Thank you to every player who reported a problem. ## Getting started 1. Download the Mac or Windows launcher from [s2arm.com](https://s2arm.com) and open it. 2. Import your own keys and games; put the base game, updates and DLC in one folder and import them together. 3. Connect your iPhone, click Install S2Arm on the S2Arm tile, first in the launcher's game library, sign in and sign with your Apple ID, and S2Arm goes onto your phone. 4. Pick a game and click Push to iPhone. 5. Open S2Arm on your phone and pick a game in the library. You can also play on the Mac itself: choose This Mac. Without a cable, export a .s2arm file and put it on your phone with AirDrop or the Files app. ### Self-signing with AltStore / SideStore Import games right on your phone, with no Apple ID sign-in on a computer and no new certificate: 1. In AltStore or SideStore settings, export your signing certificate and set a password. 2. Open S2Arm: gear → Signing certificate → Import .p12…, pick the certificate and enter the password. 3. Then put .s2arm and .img files (exported from your computer or shared by a friend) into S2Arm's Import Here folder, and play. Note: manage each Apple ID from AltServer on only one computer. Using two makes them revoke each other's certificates, and AltStore shows "Multiple AltServers". Before the 7 days run out, just tap Refresh All in AltStore; nothing else to do in S2Arm. ### Upgrading from 0.5 The games, saves and game data already on your phone all stay. No exporting again, no sending game data again. 1. On a Mac, sign in with your Apple ID once in S2Arm (0.5 used the account signed in to Xcode; 0.6.0 signs in inside S2Arm. Windows players skip this step). 2. Connect your phone and click Update S2Arm on the S2Arm tile, first in the game library. Your saves are backed up to the computer first, then the new app goes on over the old one (same Apple ID). 3. Right after that, the same page says how many old games on this phone need one update before they play; they are all checked, so click Update these N games (or later, check the games marked Update suggested in the dashboard and click Update selected). One game at a time, it brings the saves back to the computer, pushes the new program and sends only the resources that changed; each game takes about 1–2 minutes. For games whose shader library was built by the old version, the computer rebuilds it with the new one in this step (the game's files or its Mac version must still be in your library); the first time takes from a few minutes to a few tens of minutes. You don't need S-grade optimization for this. On a Windows PC without the Metal developer tools, this step sends the old library and says why; the game still plays, and once you install them under Get this PC ready, push again to get the new library. Until step 3 is done those games show Update once on your computer on the phone and won't open, but they aren't gone. Games installed from another computer are listed on a separate line on the same page; update them on that computer. If you used Free up space to delete a game's iPhone resource pack, build that game's iPhone package again. If you sign the app yourself with AltStore or similar: connect the phone, click Install S2Arm on the S2Arm card first in the game library, and on the page saying you aren't signed in with an Apple ID, click Export for self-signing instead (no iPhone needed) to get the new S2Arm.ipa; install it over the old one with AltStore; import your signing certificate (SideStore: gear → Signing certificate → Get from SideStore in S2Arm; AltStore: export it in AltStore settings, then Import .p12…); finally click Send selected to iPhone in the console, or click Export for self-signing on each game and put its .s2arm and .img into Import Here. ## Let an AI drive Both the Mac and Windows launchers expose a control interface, `s2armctl`. An AI assistant can import games, build, install, follow progress and read errors, and every step shows up in the launcher window. A companion self-check, self-fix and feedback toolkit lets the AI find a problem, apply the documented fix, and, when it cannot, package a diagnostic bundle for you to file. Watch an AI diagnose and fix a real problem end to end: [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#ai-at-the-wheel) ### Have an AI do it for you Send this to your AI assistant (it needs to be able to run commands on your computer): > Please read https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/blob/main/launchers/macos/skill/s2arm-operator/SKILL.md and then help me install my Switch game on my iPhone. It moves forward with a few commands, and you can watch every step in the launcher window: ```bash /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl start # open and connect to the launcher /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl next # what to do now, who does it, and why /Applications/S2Arm.app/Contents/Resources/s2armctl diag export ~/Desktop/S2Arm-diagnostics.zip # export a diagnostic bundle if it cannot fix a problem ``` Anything only you can do (system permission prompts, signing in with your Apple ID, tapping Trust on your phone), the AI stops and asks you to do. On Windows, use `s2armctl.cmd` in the launcher folder with the same commands. Windows builds iPhone / iPad packages only, so report problems inside a game from the phone: tap the report button to the right of the gear at the top left in game and say which game, what you did and what you saw. The diagnostic bundle is uploaded with it. **Something wrong inside a game** (graphics, frame rate, stutter, crashes)? Send your AI: > Please read https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/blob/main/skills/player-game-triage/SKILL.md . My S2Arm game has this problem: . Check the settings first, then collect diagnostics; if you can change code, fix it at the root and open a PR, otherwise help me file an issue. ## Tested at scale **211** games surveyed with a **95%** first-try build success rate. **4,700+** test runs on real iOS devices and **1,000+** on macOS. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#tested-at-scale) ## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery On a 16 GB MacBook Air (M3), from importing a game to a finished iPhone build, completely cold: | Game | Game files | Shaders | Build time | |---|---|---|---| | A 23.5 GB action RPG | 23.5 GB | 1,222 | **6.4 min** | | A 12.0 GB life-sim game | 12.0 GB | 9,315 | **8.6 min** | | A 17.5 GB open-world game | 17.5 GB | 26,999 | **34 min** | A Switch 2 game, measured on an iPhone 17 Pro Max: a **full 60 fps** while the phone is cool, **37–43 fps** once sustained load has heated it up, at about **0.15 J per frame**. [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#speed-and-efficiency) ## Platforms | Platform | Support | |---|---| | iPhone / iPad | iOS / iPadOS 18 and later; every game in one S2Arm app | | Mac | Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later; the launcher installs the app and sends games, and you can also play on the Mac | | Windows | Graphical launcher: install the app, send games, export .s2arm | [Evidence](docs/validation/EVIDENCE.md#platforms) ## Downstream deep ports Some games have a deep port made specially by the community. S2Arm recognizes these games: on export it shows a page explaining the option, and you can switch to the downstream project's route (importing, packing and installing are still buttons in S2Arm, with the downstream project's implementation underneath) or keep the standard route. The registry is [`pack/downstream/schemes.json`](pack/downstream/schemes.json); the contract between the two is the downstream project's document. | Route | Project | Devices | Contract | |---|---|---|---| | D2R-Mobile | [jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) | iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; Android and HarmonyOS in progress) | [docs/S2ARM.md](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile/blob/main/docs/S2ARM.md) | ## Honest boundaries S2Arm runs 64-bit (AArch64) games. Apple silicon cannot execute 32-bit ARM code, so 32-bit games are outside what S2Arm supports, as are games that need a 36-bit address space. ## Development [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [AI collaboration policy](LLM_POLICY.md) · [Diagnosis and root-fix skills for AI](skills/) · [Report a problem](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/S2Arm/issues) · [Third-party licenses](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md) ## Thanks S2Arm stands on the shoulders of its community. - **Co-developers**: thank you to everyone who has opened a pull request or issue in this project. Yogurt
Private AI meeting notes, with no bot in your call.
A free, open-source alternative to Granola, Otter and Fireflies.

Website · GitHub
## Introduction Yogurt records your microphone and call audio, then transcribes and summarizes on your Mac, Windows or Linux computer. It names speakers from Zoom, Teams and Meet and answers questions across meetings with sources. ## Why Our conversations are our business. We want our meeting notes on our own computers, with no account to create. That's why we built Yogurt to record, transcribe and summarize locally. It goes online only to download models and check for updates. ## Download Yogurt is free for [Mac](https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/releases/latest/download/Yogurt-mac-arm64.dmg), [Windows](https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/releases/latest/download/Yogurt-windows-x64.exe) and [Linux](https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/releases/latest/download/Yogurt-linux-x86_64.AppImage). On a Mac you can also use [Homebrew](https://brew.sh). ```sh brew install --cask frigadehq/yogurt/yogurt ``` ## What it does - **Live transcripts.** Yogurt records calls and turns speech into text as you talk. - **Meeting summaries.** Yogurt writes up the conversation and any notes you add. - **Private by default.** Your audio, transcripts and AI processing stay on your computer. - **Free and open source.** You can use Yogurt without an account. - **Who said what.** Yogurt names speakers from Zoom, Teams and Meet on Mac, Windows and Linux. - **Languages.** Multi-language mode transcribes 99 languages, follows each side of the call in its own language, and keeps up when someone switches languages mid-meeting. - **Recording reminders.** Yogurt offers to record when a supported call starts. - **Answers with sources.** Yogurt answers questions across meetings and links to the source. - **Folders and search.** You can find meetings by folder, title, notes or transcript. - **Copy and export.** You can copy notes or transcripts, or save both as Markdown. - **Local MCP server.** When you turn this on, apps on your computer can read your notes, transcripts, saved audio and each meeting's calendar details (attendees' names and emails). - **Automatic stop.** By default, Yogurt stops recording when it detects that your call has ended. A recording you start yourself with New note asks first instead, since it may not be a call. ## Watch the demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da16b894-beb1-491a-89e1-fd10666dc9b8 ## How it works 1. **Record.** Start recording your microphone and call audio; you can add your own notes. 2. **Transcribe.** Yogurt uses whisper.cpp and, on supported Macs, Apple SpeechAnalyzer. 3. **Summarize and ask.** A local open-weight model runs through llama.cpp. Meeting data stays local; Yogurt goes online for model downloads and update checks.
Where your meetings, recordings, settings and models are stored - Mac uses `~/Library/Application Support/Yogurt`. - Windows uses `%APPDATA%\Yogurt`. - Linux uses `~/.config/Yogurt`, or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Yogurt` if set.
## FAQ
What kind of computer do I need?
> A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14.4 or newer, a 64-bit PC with Windows 10 (version 2004) or newer, or a 64-bit Linux computer with Ubuntu 22.04 or newer. Each needs at least 8 GB of memory. If your computer is too slow, Yogurt tells you during setup. On Windows and Linux, you connect your calendar with a private calendar link.
Does Yogurt join my meetings?
> No. Yogurt records your microphone and the sound playing on your computer. No bot joins the call, so let the other people on the call know you’re recording.
Are recordings saved?
> Audio is saved by default, and you can turn this off for future meetings in Settings.
Is Yogurt free?
> Yes. Yogurt is free and open source under the MIT license. No account is needed.
Does Yogurt work offline?
> Yes. After a one-time download of the AI models, transcription and summaries run locally on your computer.
Does Yogurt train AI on my meetings? Can anyone at Yogurt read them?
> No. Your recordings, transcripts and notes stay on your computer, and Yogurt has no server that receives them, so nobody at Yogurt can read them. The AI models run on your computer and don't learn from your meetings. Yogurt only goes online to download its models, check for updates and, if you add one, read your calendar link.
Is Yogurt safe for confidential meetings?
> Yogurt keeps everything on your computer: audio, transcripts and notes are never uploaded, and transcription and summaries run offline. That makes it a good fit for client calls, therapy sessions, legal work and board meetings where audio can't go to a cloud service. You can also turn off saving audio in **Settings**, and Yogurt is open source, so anyone can check what it does. Follow your own rules on getting consent to record.
How much memory do I need?
> At least 8 GB. Yogurt checks your computer during setup and picks the best transcription and notes models it can run well. With 16 GB or more, Yogurt can usually run a larger notes model that writes better notes.
Can I turn an existing recording into notes?
> Yes. Use **Upload a file** to add an MP3, M4A or WAV recording. Yogurt transcribes it on your computer and writes notes, the same as for a live meeting.
Can I ask questions across all my meetings?
> Yes. Use **Ask** to ask about one meeting, a folder, or all your meetings at once, for example "what did we decide about pricing?". Answers point to the meetings they came from, and everything runs on your computer.
How accurate is it compared to cloud transcription?
> Yogurt uses Whisper large-v3-turbo on computers that can run it, the same family of models many cloud services use, so English accuracy is close to cloud transcription. Smaller computers get a smaller Whisper model, which is faster but makes more mistakes, especially outside English. You can add names and words to a custom vocabulary so they're spelled right.
How much does setup download?
> It depends on your computer. Yogurt sets up transcription first, then downloads the notes models selected for your computer. Recording works once setup finishes, and notes and questions work offline once the notes model is in.
How do I connect my assistant app?
> In **Settings → AI apps**, turn on access, copy the helper command, and add it as a local MCP server in your assistant app. Access is off by default. The app can read your meetings (including their calendar details: the event, and attendees' names and emails), notes and transcripts, but cannot change them. It may send what it reads to its own online model. Turn access off in Yogurt to stop further reads.
Can other apps read my notes through MCP?
> Access is off until you enable it in **Settings → AI apps**. Apps get read-only access to meetings (with their calendar event and attendees' names and emails), notes and transcripts. Mac and Linux use a socket in your profile folder with `0600` permissions, so only your user account can open it. Windows uses a named pipe with a new random name each launch, stored only in your profile folder. There is no per-app token, so any app running under your account can read while access is on. Settings shows connected apps by their self-reported names.
Which AI models does Yogurt use?
> Transcription uses Whisper through whisper.cpp, with large-v3-turbo or a smaller model depending on your computer. On supported Macs, Apple SpeechAnalyzer supplies live words while Whisper produces the saved transcript. Summaries and answers use a local open-weight model from the Gemma 4, gpt-oss or Qwen3 families, chosen for your hardware and run through llama.cpp. The app uses Electron and needs no account.
Which languages does Yogurt support?
> Pick **Multi-language** in **Settings → Language → Spoken language** to transcribe 99 languages. You can also switch from the **English** menu in a note’s footer before or during recording. English only is the default, and it’s the fastest and most accurate choice for English meetings. > > In Multi-language mode, you and the other side of the call can each speak your own language, and Yogurt follows along when someone switches languages mid-meeting. Summaries follow the meeting’s main language, or the one you pick in **Settings → Summary language**. Answers in Ask follow your question’s language. Settings also offers 32 app languages.
Which call apps does Yogurt work with?
> You can record calls in any app because Yogurt captures your microphone and system audio. Call detection covers Zoom, Teams and Meet. On Mac, Yogurt can also read their speaker names with Accessibility permission, when the call app shows who is speaking.
How does Yogurt know a call has started?
> It checks which apps are using your microphone. For browser calls, it also checks the tab title or a nearby calendar event with a call link. This triggers an offer to record; recording starts only when you choose to.
How do I connect my calendar?
> On Mac, allow Calendar access in Settings. Yogurt reads the calendars already on your computer and lets you choose which ones to show. You do not sign into a calendar account in Yogurt.
## Support - [Help](docs/README.md) - [Discord](https://yogurt.so/discord) - [Report a bug](https://github.com/FrigadeHQ/yogurt/issues) ## Development - [Build and run locally](docs/building.md) --- Made by [Frigade](https://frigade.com?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=yogurt), [MIT license](LICENSE).

title: Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
author: Jakeschincariol
body:
# The Replica skill

Eleven Claude skills that clone any app. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key,
nothing to connect.

One reverse-engineers the app you want to clone. One rebuilds it. One tests it
for bugs. And one is the Entrepreneur: it reads what the app's users hate and
fixes it in yours, so you have an app you can sell.

In between, the others plan the stack and the database, rebuild the design
system, wire up auth and payments, score your clone against the original, give
it a name and a brand of its own, write the landing page and the store
listing, and put it live on your domain.

**It rebuilds what an app does, never what it owns.** Features and flows,
clean-room style. Not its code, its logo, its copy or its content. The
fine print is at the bottom, and the skills enforce it.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
/plugin install replica-skill@replica-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/replica-skill:replica-recon` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/replica-recon`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.git
cp -r replica-skill/replica-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the
method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/replica-recon` | Reverse-engineers any app: screens, flows, components, data model. From public pages, screenshots, store listings and your own account. |
| `/replica-architect` | Plans the stack, database schema and API for your clone. |
| `/replica-design` | Rebuilds the design system: colours, type, spacing, components. As tokens, with your own assets. |
| `/replica-build` | Rebuilds the app screen by screen from the recon map. |
| `/replica-backend` | Auth, database, payments and integrations. |
| `/replica-test` | Clicks through every flow and tests it for bugs. |
| `/replica-diff` | Compares your clone against the original. A parity score and what is missing. |
| `/replica-entrepreneur` | Reads what the app's users hate in real reviews and turns it into fixes and a positioning angle. |
| `/replica-brand` | Names and rebrands your version so it is yours. |
| `/replica-launch` | Landing page, pricing and App Store listing. |
| `/replica-deploy` | Ships it live on your own domain. |

## How to use it

Run them in order. Each one reads what the last one wrote, in a `replica/`
folder in your project.

```
recon -> architect -> design -> build -> backend -> test -> diff -> entrepreneur -> brand -> launch -> deploy
```

An example: cloning a scheduling app, the kind where you share a link and
people book a time with you.

1. **`/replica-recon`** with the app's URL. It reads the help center, the
   pricing page, the store listing and public walkthroughs, and you click
   through your own account with it. Out comes `replica/recon.md`: 18
   screens, 7 flows (guest books a meeting, host sets availability, guest
   reschedules...), the components, an inferred data model (users, event
   types, availability, bookings) and `features.csv`. The partner
   marketplace is marked out of scope: that is their network, not a feature.
2. **`/replica-architect`** picks Next.js, Postgres, Stripe and Resend, writes
   the schema (with a constraint so two guests can never book the same slot)
   and orders the build: the booking flow end to end first.
3. **`/replica-design`** measures the screenshots into tokens: colour roles,
   type scale, 8px spacing, the date picker and slot button specs. Open
   icons, an open font, your own words.
4. **`/replica-build`** builds the shell, then the booking flow, then every
   screen with all its states, ticking off `features.csv` as it goes.
5. **`/replica-backend`** adds sign up, Google Calendar through Google's own
   API with your keys, Stripe for paid bookings, reminder emails.
6. **`/replica-test`** writes a test plan from the 7 flows, Playwright specs
   for the happy paths and edge cases (time zones, a slot taken mid-booking,
   double submit), and logs bugs by severity until no S1 or S2 is open.
7. **`/replica-diff`** scores it. Features 86, all must-haves done, booking
   page layout 91. Missing: round-robin for teams, the website embed.
8. **`/replica-entrepreneur`** reads 140 real reviews across the App Store,
   G2, Capterra and Reddit. Top complaints: per-seat price jumps, no text
   reminders, guests confused by time zones. Each with counts and linked
   quotes. Fix plan: flat pricing, SMS reminders, a time zone confirm step.
   Angle: booking links for small teams that hate per-seat pricing.
9. **`/replica-brand`** names it (with the trademark and domain checks to
   run), gives it a new palette, a logo brief and a voice, then sweeps the
   codebase until nothing of the original is left.
10. **`/replica-launch`** writes the landing page around the angle, sets
    pricing against the original's public page, and lints the store listing.
11. **`/replica-deploy`** runs the preflight (tests, parity, sweep, listing),
    sets up production, gives you the DNS records for your domain, and ships
    it when you say go.

You can also run any one on its own. `/replica-entrepreneur` on an app you
are only thinking about cloning is a good way to find out if you should.

## The tools

Six of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.

```bash
python3 replica-diff/imgdiff.py original.png clone.png --out diff.png   # layout diff, ignores colour
python3 replica-diff/parity.py replica/features.csv                     # parity score + missing list
python3 replica-entrepreneur/reviews.py replica/reviews.csv             # what users hate, ranked, linked
python3 replica-design/contrast.py replica/design/tokens.json           # WCAG contrast on your tokens
python3 replica-brand/sweep.py . --avoid "Original App"                 # anything of the original left?
python3 replica-launch/listing.py replica/launch/listing.json           # store limits + copycat checks
```

**`imgdiff.py`** reads PNGs with no libraries, turns both screenshots into
edge maps and compares where things are, so your new colours do not count
against you. It tells you which regions differ, in the original's pixels.

**`parity.py`** weights must, should and could, counts partial as half, and
never scores what you left out on purpose or what you added. Missing
must-haves means not shippable, and it says so.

**`reviews.py`** drops every review without a link. Every quote it prints is
copied from a row you gave it, with that row's URL. Themes with under three
reviews or one source are marked thin.

**`sweep.py`** finds the original's name, domain and colours anywhere in your
code, including inside identifiers like `OriginalAppEmbed`, and blocks the
deploy until it is clean.

**`listing.py`** checks App Store and Google Play limits, ranking claims in
the title, wasted keyword characters, and the original's name anywhere in
your listing.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Fine print

**It rebuilds functionality and UX patterns, clean-room style.** It studies
what the app does and how people move through it, then writes everything
fresh. It never copies the target's source code, proprietary assets, logos,
trademarks, copy or private APIs.

**It only reads what you are allowed to read.** Public pages and your own
account. It never scrapes behind a login or against a site's terms, never
logs into anyone else's account, and never gets past a paywall. If your
account's terms forbid using it to build a competitor, it says so and sticks
to public sources.

**It always rebrands before launch.** New name, new palette, new logo, new
words. `/replica-deploy` will not ship until the sweep is clean.

**"Clone any app" means the features and the flow.** Not the content, the
network or the licences an app owns. You can rebuild a music app's player,
playlists and sharing. You cannot clone its catalogue.

**No guarantee of a "perfect" clone.** Results depend on how complex the app
is. A booking tool is weeks. A spreadsheet engine is not. `/replica-recon`
sizes it honestly before you start, and `/replica-diff` gives you a real
number, not a vibe.

**The Entrepreneur never makes things up.** No invented reviews, quotes or
numbers. Every claim has a link, and the sample size is stated.

**Check before you sell.** Run the trademark checks `/replica-brand` lists,
read the terms of anything you used, and talk to a lawyer before launch if
there is money on the line. This is not legal advice.

## Files

```
replica-recon/         SKILL.md, recon-map.md, features.csv (the matrix template)
replica-architect/     SKILL.md, architecture.md
replica-design/        SKILL.md, tokens.json, contrast.py
replica-build/         SKILL.md
replica-backend/       SKILL.md
replica-test/          SKILL.md, test-plan.md, bug-report.md, e2e.example.spec.ts
replica-diff/          SKILL.md, imgdiff.py, parity.py
replica-entrepreneur/  SKILL.md, reviews.py, themes.json
replica-brand/         SKILL.md, sweep.py
replica-launch/        SKILL.md, listing.py, listing.example.json
replica-deploy/        SKILL.md, preflight.md
tests/                 the tests for every tool
```

Your own files live in `replica/` in your project. The skills read each
other's.

## Credit

Made by Jake Schincariol, [opusjake.ai](https://opusjake.ai). Siblings:
[Arena](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/arena-skill),
[X](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/x-agent-skill),
[LinkedIn](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/linkedin-agent-skill),
[Instagram](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill).

## License

MIT. Take it, change it, ship it.
