title: marcelodosreis/sassy
author: marcelodosreis
body:
Sassy

Welcome to **Sassy**, a powerful template generator designed to accelerate the development of Micro-SaaS applications. Built with **Next.js 15**, **TypeScript**, **TailwindCSS**, **Supabase**, and **Stripe**, Sassy provides a robust foundation for building subscription-based services with integrated authentication, subscription management, and payment processing. | **Feature** | **Status** | |-----------------------------------------|------------| | OAuth Authentication (Google, FB, Twitter) | ✅ | | Subscription & Billing (Stripe) | ✅ | | Free Trial Periods (Stripe) | ✅ | | Billing Portal (Stripe) | ✅ | | Webhooks for Stripe Events | ✅ | | Subscriptions & Payments API Routes | ✅ | | User Authentication (Supabase) | ✅ | | E-Mail (Mailgun) | ✅ | | Personalized Dashboard | ✅ | | Responsive Design + Landing Page | ✅ | | Logs & Monitoring (Datadog) | ✅ | You can learn more about the other features by visiting the following documentation page: [Sassy Documentation](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/develop/docs). We are constantly improving Sassy with new features to make it even more powerful. You can find the current roadmap and planned features on our [Feature Roadmap](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/develop/docs/feature-roadmap.md) ## Architecture and Structure Sassy's architecture is designed to streamline the rapid development of Micro-SaaS applications by providing essential features like user authentication, subscription management, and seamless payment processing. The project structure is clean and organized to help developers get started quickly while maintaining flexibility and scalability. ### Project Structure: ```bash src/ ├── app/ # Main logic and core functionality of the application ├── components/ # Reusable UI components ├── constants/ # Global constants and configurations ├── contexts/ # React contexts for global state management ├── hooks/ # Custom React hooks ├── libs/ # Third-party libraries and utilities ├── pages/ # Next.js pages corresponding to routes │ └── api/ # API routes for backend functionality ├── services/ # External API integrations and services ├── styles/ # TailwindCSS configuration and custom styles ├── utils/ # Utility functions and helpers └── middleware.ts # Middleware for request processing ``` ### Integration with Supabase and Stripe: - **Supabase** is used for user authentication and real-time database management. The `subscriptions` table is created to store subscription-related data for each user. - **Stripe** is integrated to handle payment processing and subscription plan management. ### SQL Script for Creating the `subscriptions` Table in Supabase: ```sql CREATE TABLE subscriptions ( id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(), user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, stripe_subscription_id TEXT UNIQUE, plan TEXT CHECK (plan IN ('free', 'starter', 'creator', 'pro')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free', status TEXT CHECK (status IN ('active', 'canceled', 'past_due', 'incomplete', 'trialing')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', current_period_start TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, current_period_end TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE, created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() ); ``` > **Note:** Since subscription data is sensitive, ensure that **Row Level Security (RLS)** is disabled for the `subscriptions` table. ### Environment Configuration: The environment variables are configured to integrate Sassy with Supabase and Stripe. Make sure to update the values accordingly. ```env NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_URL= NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY= NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL= NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY= NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_APPLICATION_ID= NEXT_PUBLIC_DATADOG_CLIENT_TOKEN= SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY= STRIPE_SECRET_KEY= STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET= DATADOG_SECRET_KEY= MAILGUN_SECRET_KEY= MAILGUN_SECRET_DOMAIN= ``` > **Note:** Replace the above values with your own Supabase and Stripe keys. ## Key Features - **Authentication with Supabase:** Utilize Supabase for user authentication, providing a secure and scalable login system. - **Subscription Management with Stripe:** Easily manage different subscription plans, handle payments, and track user subscriptions with Stripe integration. - **Responsive Design with TailwindCSS:** The application uses TailwindCSS for styling, ensuring a modern and responsive design out of the box. - **Built-in API Routes:** Ready-to-use API routes for managing subscriptions, payments, and user data. - **OAuth Support:** The app supports OAuth login via **Google**, **Facebook**, and **Twitter**, providing users with a seamless authentication experience. --- ## Webhook Listener for Stripe To handle incoming webhooks from Stripe (such as subscription updates, payment failures, etc.), Sassy includes a script for listening to Stripe webhooks: ```bash pnpm stripe:listen ``` This script connects your local environment to Stripe and listens for events like **invoice.payment_succeeded**, **invoice.payment_failed**, and more. It will automatically trigger the corresponding handler in your application to process the events. > **Note:** When using this in your development environment, make sure you have the Stripe secret key and webhook secret configured in your `.env.local` file. --- ## OAuth Authentication Sassy comes with built-in OAuth authentication support for popular platforms such as **Google**, **Facebook**, and **Twitter**. The authentication flow is fully integrated with Supabase, ensuring a secure and seamless experience for users. ### Dependencies: - OAuth SDKs for Google, Facebook, and Twitter to provide login functionality. With **OAuth**, users can authenticate with their preferred social media accounts, reducing friction in the signup/login process. OAuth tokens are securely managed by Supabase, and user data is synchronized across both Supabase and your application. > **Note:** The OAuth login functionality is already set up and fully supported out of the box. If you're using different authentication providers, you can easily extend this functionality by following the Supabase OAuth documentation. --- ## Setup Instructions ### 1. Install Dependencies Ensure that you have **pnpm** installed. If not, install it globally: ```bash npm install -g pnpm ``` Then, install the project dependencies: ```bash pnpm install ``` ### 2. Set Up Environment Variables Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory of the project and add the necessary environment variables (as provided in the **Environment Configuration** section). ### 3. Run the Development Server Once the environment is set up, start the development server: ```bash pnpm dev ``` The application will be available at `http://localhost:3000`. ### 4. Database Configuration To set up your Supabase project, run the provided SQL script to create the `subscriptions` table in your Supabase database. ### 5. Stripe Integration Make sure your Stripe API keys are correctly set up. You can test the payment processing using Stripe’s test keys in a sandbox environment. --- ## Development vs Production Environments For **development** and **production**, Sassy uses separate Supabase projects to ensure a clean and isolated environment. This allows you to safely test changes in the development environment without affecting live data in production. > **Note:** Ensure that you configure your `.env.local` with the correct Supabase project URL and keys for each environment. --- ## Conclusion Sassy provides a solid foundation for developing subscription-based Micro-SaaS applications. By leveraging the power of **Next.js**, **Supabase**, **Stripe**, **OAuth**, and **TailwindCSS**, you can rapidly build and deploy secure and scalable applications. Whether you're just starting a new SaaS product or iterating on an existing idea, Sassy makes it easy to focus on what matters most: delivering value to your users. --- For more information on integrating **Stripe**, **Supabase**, and **OAuth**, refer to the official documentation: - [Stripe Documentation](https://stripe.com/docs) - [Supabase Documentation](https://supabase.com/docs) - [OAuth Integration Guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-helpers/oauth) - [Sassy Integration with Datadog](https://github.com/marcelodosreis/sassy/blob/main/docs/datadog.md)

# Backlink Pilot v3

An AI Agent playbook for paced directory and list backlinks: free / free-queue by default, treat reciprocal links, badges, and ownership checks as configurable costs, and grow a reusable site library.

[中文](README.zh.md) · [Docs home](docs/index.md) · [Full guide](docs/guide.md) · Agent runbook [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) · Legacy CLI branch [`old`](https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot/tree/old) (v2.1)

---

## What it is

**Backlink Pilot** is an **AI Agent playbook** (Grok Bot and others) for directory / list outreach — not a black-box “submit hundreds in one command” script.

| Version | Contents |
|---------|----------|
| **v3 (this branch `main`)** | Strategy tiers, daily caps, email loop, `/links`, library ledger, risk notes; human README + agent runbook [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) |
| **v2.1 (branch [`old`](https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot/tree/old))** | Legacy CLI: OpenClaw / Claude Code / bb-browser / Playwright toolkit |

**In the repo:** method docs, empty templates (product card with media fields, library CSV, `/links` example, [assets](docs/assets.md) checklist), historical `targets.yaml` (**unmaintained**).  
**Not in the repo:** runnable batch-submit CLI (see `old`), real submit logs, passwords / cookies, filled directory lists.

---

## What it's for

After you ship an indie product, you often want links from **directories, free-queue launches, and resource / awesome lists**. Forms differ; many need login, captcha, scheduling, and email verification. The hard part is **policy judgment + email loop + pacing**, not filling one form.

This project helps you:

1. **Set rules** — Conservative / Standard / Aggressive; default **Standard** (free & free-queue; optional badge and domain ownership OK; skip paid and required reciprocals by default)
2. **Pace work** — about **2–4 real submissions per day**; scout in bulk, submit slowly
3. **Reuse** — a library ledger of site attributes and per-product status so the next product hits validated sites first
4. **Hand off cleanly** — humans handle DNS/meta, domain mail, paid/tier exceptions; agents research, submit, click verifies, and bookkeep
5. **State the risk** — directory link value varies; volume ≠ rankings (see Disclaimer below)

It is **not** a ranking promise, a link-buying guide, or a tutorial on evading search enforcement.

---

## How to use

### For humans

**Shortest path:**

1. Read [Notes](#notes注意事项) and [Disclaimer](#disclaimer免责声明) (full text: [docs/disclaimer.md](docs/disclaimer.md))
2. Copy [templates/product.example.yaml](templates/product.example.yaml) for your product (**location and email must match Terms / Privacy**)
3. **Prep a media pack:** square logo (prefer transparent), OG (~1200×630), desktop/mobile screenshots, optional banner / promo video, plus short/long slogan variants. Checklist: [docs/assets.md](docs/assets.md); put paths on the product card
4. Copy [templates/library.schema.csv](templates/library.schema.csv) locally (e.g. `library.filled.csv`); **do not commit filled ledgers**
5. Optionally add a `/links` page ([templates/links-page.example.md](templates/links-page.example.md); docs: [reciprocity](docs/reciprocity.md))
6. Paste [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) (or the English block in [templates/agent-prompt.md](templates/agent-prompt.md)) into the Agent’s system / project instructions; set tier (recommend Standard) and daily cap 2–4
7. Give the Agent an inbox for signup verifies; keep domain `support@` for yourself

**What humans must do (the Agent should stop and ask):**

| Task | Why |
|------|-----|
| DNS TXT / page meta ownership | Touches your domain or production site |
| Verify links in a domain mailbox | Agent often cannot read that inbox |
| Paid boost / Featured | Forbidden on Standard by default |
| Required reciprocal, badge-required-to-submit, upvote-for-credits | Policy exceptions |
| Change location / email after rejection | May touch legal pages |
| Captcha / 2FA / unauthorized bulk GitHub PRs | Account & compliance |
| Final logo / OG / screenshots / video | Design & brand; Agent only checks and uploads |

Setup: [docs/agent-setup.md](docs/agent-setup.md) · Grok Bot case (fictional Northstar Notes): [docs/grok-bot.md](docs/grok-bot.md) · Full guide: [docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md)

Want local Chrome scripts / old adapters? Check out [`old`](https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot/tree/old) — [migrating-from-v2](docs/migrating-from-v2.md).

### Verified agents

**Only Grok Bot is verified on v3 (`main`)** (through 2026-10). Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, DeepSeek-family agents, Cursor Cloud Agent, ChatGPT / Custom GPT alone, OpenClaw, and similar runtimes have **not** had a systematic smoke test of “read AGENTS.md + templates → submit / email loop.”

Docs are designed to be agent-agnostic (markdown runbook + templates), but **unverified ≠ proven to follow them**. Criteria, full matrix, and how that differs from branch `old` (v2.1 CLI toolkit targets): [docs/verified-agents.md](docs/verified-agents.md).

If you tried any Agent with this playbook (including ones still listed as unverified), please open an [Issue](https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot/issues) or PR: could it follow `AGENTS`, where did it stick, and did it respect the daily cap and human gates? If it meets the verification criteria, send a PR per the checklist at the end of [docs/verified-agents.md](docs/verified-agents.md) to mark that Agent verified (no filled ledgers, real site lists, passwords, or cookies). Doc, template, and translation fixes are welcome too — see [docs/contributing.md](docs/contributing.md).

### For agents

**Canonical runbook: [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)** (Chinese: [`AGENTS.zh.md`](AGENTS.zh.md)). Summary:

| Item | Default |
|------|---------|
| Tier | **Standard** |
| Real submits / day | **2–4** (scouting does not count) |
| Allow | free, free-queue; optional badge for dofollow; meta/DNS verify after human adds tokens |
| Skip | paid; required reciprocal; upvote-for-credits; dead; fit mismatch |
| Roles | Research tags → submit (prefer HTTP/API) → email triage → local CSV |
| Media | Before submit, verify product-card paths; if required image/video missing → skip or ask ([assets](docs/assets.md)) |
| Ask human | Paid, required reciprocal/badge, upvote-for-credits, legal location, domain mail, DNS/meta, rejection resubmit, unauthorized bulk PRs, new design exports |
| Report | Counts + reasons for submitted / pending / skipped; no third-party URL spam unless asked |

Product fields: [product-template](docs/product-template.md) · Library: [library](docs/library.md) · Email: [email](docs/email.md) · Funnel: [funnel](docs/funnel.md)

### Doc map

| Doc | Topic |
|-----|--------|
| [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) | Agent runbook |
| [docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md) | Full playbook |
| [docs/strategy.md](docs/strategy.md) | Tiers & pace |
| [docs/reciprocity.md](docs/reciprocity.md) | Reciprocal · badge · `/links` |
| [docs/library.md](docs/library.md) | Library ledger |
| [docs/assets.md](docs/assets.md) | Logo / OG / screenshots / video / slogans |
| [docs/verified-agents.md](docs/verified-agents.md) | Which Agents are verified (Grok Bot only for now) |
| [docs/disclaimer.md](docs/disclaimer.md) | Full disclaimer |
| [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | Pitfalls (anonymized) |

---

## Notes（注意事项）

1. **Pace:** Prefer about 2–4 real submissions per day; do not treat tens or hundreds of signups/submits in a day as recommended.
2. **Tiers:** Public docs default to **Standard**; skip required reciprocals; optional badges and ownership verify are OK. See [strategy](docs/strategy.md).
3. **`/links`:** Host reciprocals and badges on a dedicated page, not in homepage body copy; required reciprocals only after you raise the tier.
4. **Library:** Keep filled CSVs local; this repo ships an empty header only. `targets.yaml` is a historical idea pool — **not guaranteed submittable**.
5. **Honesty:** Accurate product copy; matching categories; location / entity / email consistent with legal pages or expect rejection.
6. **Media:** Most sites want logo / OG / screenshots and sometimes video; wrong ratio or size gets rejected. Humans export; Agents pick files per site. See [docs/assets.md](docs/assets.md).
7. **Secrets:** Do not commit passwords, cookies, verify tokens, or filled ledgers (see `.gitignore`).
8. **GitHub lists:** Read CONTRIBUTING first; no bulk PRs without the account owner’s authorization.
9. **Blog-comment batching:** Lives only on branch `old`; not promoted in v3.

## Disclaimer（免责声明）

- Search engines (including Google) have long discouraged **link schemes meant to manipulate rankings**. Short bursts of large-scale, low-relevance, or patterned backlinks can be treated as spam or trigger enforcement.
- Links are judged by quality and source; directory links vary widely. **Volume ≠ rankings.** This project **promises no** traffic or ranking outcomes.
- This repo is a workflow playbook — **not** a black-hat guide and not instructions on “how to evade” search actions.
- You are responsible for site behavior and outcomes from using this playbook; authors and maintainers accept no liability for loss.

Read the full page: [docs/disclaimer.md](docs/disclaimer.md). Official materials: [Google Search documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs) (official text wins).

# 🌻 Dandi API - Boilerplate for AI Micro SaaS Applications

**🤯 🤯 This repo was buikt with ENGLISH as the programming language with Cursor IDE and v0.🤯**


![Logo](https://github.com/emarco177/dandi/blob/main/public/demo.gif)

Dandi API is a comprehensive boilerplate repository for building AI-powered micro SaaS applications. It provides a solid foundation with essential components and functionalities needed to run an end-to-end micro SaaS application.

The service itself offers powerful insights, summaries, and analytics for open source GitHub repositories.

**🌐 Live Application: [https://www.dandi.cloud/](https://www.dandi.cloud/)**



## 🚀 Key Features

- **Complete Micro SaaS Structure**: Implements all necessary components for a fully functional AI micro SaaS application.
- **API Key Management**: Built-in system for handling API keys, UI heavily inspired by [Tavily](https://www.tavily.com/).
- **Rate Limiting**: Integrated rate limiting for API protection.
- **SSO Login**: Implemented Single Sign-On functionality.
- **AI Integration**: Leverages LangChain JS for AI capabilities.

## 🛠️ Built with Cursor IDE and v0

This entire project was developed using [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/), primarily through prompting with Cursor Composer and [v0](https://v0.dev/) . As a developer without frontend or full-stack experience, this project demonstrates the power of AI-assisted development.

**ENGLISH IS THE NEW PROGRAMMING LANGUAGE.**

## 🧰 Tech Stack (TBH, Cursor did it all for me)

- **Frontend**: React, Next.js 13 (App Router), Tailwind CSS
- **Backend**: Node.js, Next.js API Routes
- **Database**: Supabase (PostgreSQL)
- **Authentication**: NextAuth.js
- **UI Components**: Shadcn UI, Radix UI
- **API**: RESTful API with rate limiting and API key authentication
- **AI**: LangChain JS 🦜🔗
- **Deployment**: Vercel 



## 🚀 Getting Started

To run this project locally, follow these steps:

1. Clone the repository:
   ```
   git clone https://github.com/emarco177/dandi.git
   cd dandi
   ```

2. Install dependencies:
   ```
   yarn install
   ```

3. Set up environment variables:
   Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory and add the necessary environment variables (refer to the Environment Variables section below).

4. Run the development server:
   ```
   yarn dev
   ```

5. Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) in your browser to see the application.

Create a `.env.local` file in the root directory with the following variables:

```
DB_URL=
DB_NAME=

NEXTAUTH_SECRET=
NEXTAUTH_URL=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=

Note: Keep your `.env.local` file secure and never commit it to version control.

```
yarn build
```

To run the production build locally:

```
yarn start

title: samuel-howell/SIM
author: samuel-howell
body:
***S**imple **I**nventory **M**anagement and **P**roduct **L**ogistics* ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1WliiC62IAnbRIjaCLDmnzPm820IfNJJl) ## **Mockups**
## **Overall Summary**

SIMPL is a micro-SaaS application that is designed to improve the efficiency and maintainability of small and medium-sized businesses’ inventory and asset management capabilities. SIMPL does this by harnessing the power of Material UI, the Google Dart codebase, the Google Flutter framework, and the Google Firebase real-time database solution to provide a streamlined, simplistic, and elegant approach to inventory management and product logistics. Some primary use cases in which SIMPL excels is verifying and storing employee information, sharing databases between employees using invite-only security measures, generating QR codes for easy item tagging and tracking, scanning an item’s QR code to perform basic inventory tasks such as viewing item details, incrementing or decrementing item quantity, and building inventory reconciliation sheets. SIMPL also generates charts tracking item quantity over time, as well as store sales, so that users can make informed decisions about which products are high performers and which products simply cut into profit margins. Furthermore, SIMPL supports importing and exporting inventory data in CSV file format for further data manipulation in popular applications such as Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.

## **What is the problem?**

In many small and medium-sized companies, inventory management is a burdensome and tedious task. Because of their size, many of these companies are unable to afford many of the more prominent inventory management applications, like Cin7 and Zoho. Furthermore, they have no need for many of the features that these applications provide, such as ecommerce integration, aftership tracking, serial number tracking, etc. These business owners simply need a way to keep track of what is in stock, what isn’t, and which items are providing the most profit. I saw this first-hand at the company I interned with in Summer 2021. Inventory reconciliation was being done by hand with paper every day. Employees would physically count the items on the shelves and mark the totals on paper to compare with what the online inventory was showing. When I asked the store supervisor about the reasoning behind hand-counting inventory, she said that she was unable to find a suitable software solution. As I began to research this issue further, trying to see if I could find a software alternative, I also started reading articles about how the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic had many reconsidering their job prospects, and how this was spurring the Great Resignation, which has led to an outgrowth of entrepreneurship and the creation of many small businesses. According to the Census Bureau, more than 4.4 million new businesses were created in the U.S. during 2020 alone. Pulling inspiration from my conversation with my supervisor, and the research I had done around inventory management software solutions, I saw a niche market and the idea of SIMPL was born. This new market of fledgling business owners and entrepreneurs has untapped potential in the realm of inventory management software, and SIMPL aims to be the answer.

## **How does SIMPL solve it?**

SIMPL will provide a service that many small and medium-sized business owners will benefit greatly from, without having to rely on any outside partnerships or external relationships. Using QR code technology in conjunction with the SIMPL app on iPhones, Androids, or Web-based devices, businesses will be able to manage their inventory in a quick and cost-efficient manner. Because SIMPL is cross-platform, it will be able to quickly integrate into a company’s workflow regardless of whether they use Apple, Android, or the Web-based devices. Also, because of CSV export capabilities, inventory data obtained through SIMPL can be shared and further analyzed through other applications if the user chooses to do so. This makes SIMPL a great addon for businesses that already have some form of inventory management in place, while also providing a competitive alternative for those who are in the market for a completely new system. SIMPL was built predominantly for phones, because we wanted to provide a cost-efficient solution for companies that didn’t want to invest in barcode scanner hardware and software. Utilizing QR code technology, as opposed to conventional barcodes, information retention capacity is greatly increased, being that a QR code has up to up to a 30% error correction capability. This means that up to 30% of the QR code can be damaged, by fading, dirt, accidental marking, scuffs, etc. and SIMPL can still read the information stored in the code. As inventory is moved between locations and endures the wear and tear of retail, this will reduce the headache that comes with inventory becoming unscannable due to damage to the barcode. Additionally, due to the more compact form of QR codes, printing costs may be decreased by up to 25% in certain use cases. Concerning logistics, SIMPL is designed to simplify communication first and foremost. Users will be able to see who last interacted with any item currently in the database. They will also be able to quickly and easily share stores with other users. Along with customary item insertion and deletion, SIMPL is designed to store scan-in and scan-out data for each item, allowing the application to generate detailed graphs concerning item quantity over a period of hours, days, months, or a year. For each store, SIMPL will also highlight which items are low in stock and which items are most popular, which will aid the user in making informed decisions about what items to purchase in the future. SIMPL also features an inventory reconciliation scan option, which will allow the user to scan the product on the physical store shelves, export that data to a separate CSV, and then compare the Official Inventory CSV to the Inventory Reconciliation CSV in order to find discrepancies quickly.

## **Who is the Target Market?**

Right now, our target market includes small to medium-sized retail companies, employing anywhere from 1 employee to 1000 employees, that either do not have an inventory management system in place, or would like to integrate a lightweight, cost-efficient addition into their current inventory management processes. With smaller businesses especially, there is a need to keep costs low. In doing so, more money can be put back into the business in the form of inventory and advertising, allowing the business to expand its profit margin and market presence. SIMPL is a solution for businesses who need inventory management and product logistics on a budget. As businesses reach those higher profit margins and bigger customer bases, inventory management becomes increasingly more important. Built with this in mind, SIMPL helps businesses establish a baseline for good inventory management practices early on, without divesting key funding that should be going to promote the business’s overall growth. We think that this affordability factor will be the main draw for customers who want to purchase and use the SIMPL software. Also, because of SIMPL’s availability on the major technology platforms (Web, Android, and iOS) we aim to be compatible with most, if not all, of the devices currently in use in our target market. Beyond our primary customer segment in retail , we would eventually like to bring SIMPL to small manufacturing companies and build a material requirement planning feature into the app, but that will depend on future development.

## **What is SIMPL's competitive advantage?**

There are a few other inventory management apps currently in the market, but, to our knowledge, none provide cross-platform support, an updated UI built to Google Material UI standards, an inventory reconciliation feature, and other streamlined features built specific to small and medium-sized businesses at a competitive price point. Many full-fledged software solutions and competitors, like Cin7, Ordoro, and Webgility, suffer from feature bloat and contain many tools that starting entrepreneurs and business owners may not need. SIMPL challenges the assumption that all of these extra features are necessary for an efficient management solution. Our research showed that features that generated Bill of Materials, Manufacturing Orders, or Purchase Orders, or integrated Point of Sale systems, were often under-utilized by many smaller business customers. Many of these bigger software options also lacked mobile apps to serve in the place of scanning hardware. Concerning the lightweight app sphere, we found that current apps such as Sortly, TookStock, and Telesto were very uniform in function, and there was not much to differentiate between them. None of these apps allowed users to see change in quantity over time graphically. Sortly was the only application that allowed QR code scanning, while TookStock was the only app that offered a semblance of inventory reconciliation. SIMPL provides these niche features while also covering the standard basics of item cataloging, item insertion/deletion, store insertion/deletion, and store share features. There seems to be an assumption that these are the only features necessary for smaller business owners. However, the entrepreneurial spirit continues to expand as COVID-19 restrictions lift and people become increasingly more independent, and they are looking for smarter and better ways to work. These future innovators and business creators need a way to manage their inventory without getting bogged down in feature bloat while still being able to integrate newer inventory technologies like QR codes, and see data in a visual way with graphs and charts. Current options in the app market don’t provide all of these features in one package, and SIMPL can fill in that gap.

## **Competitive Advantage Charts** Web Software | Mobile Apps :-------------------------:|:-------------------------: ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1LUi98ABuqQvA7joXSc2Rl4ct4XVw2tVE) | ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1LXzn2vZXhxG3M5BA5eIoUyDP5Skcvt1y)

GestaltX

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.6-blue)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-27.x-black?logo=apple)](#compatibility) [![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-SwiftUI-orange?logo=swift)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv3-blue)](LICENSE) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_ZH-CN.md) · [日本語](README_JA.md) · [한국어](README_KO.md) · [Türkçe](README_TR.md) A MobileGestalt editor for iPhone and iPad. Developed by [huamidev](https://github.com/huamidev). ## Features | Category | Presets and tools | | --- | --- | | Display | Dynamic Island capability and layout, Always-On Display, AOD Vibrancy, high-luminance AOD, AOD flipbook, HDR photo display, wallpaper parallax, Liquid Glass low-power rendering, experimental PWM and DisplayPort flags | | Device | Model name, boot/shutdown chime, charge limit, tap to wake, Camera Control settings, Action Button settings, Collision SOS, Audio Mix, Spatial FaceTime audio | | iPad | Apple Pencil settings, Stage Manager capability, iPad app compatibility | | Intelligence | Independent region-code options, Apple Intelligence capability flag, on-device Siri, Audio Intelligence, Personal Translator, Photos Clean Up, Handwriting Synthesis, always-listening Hey Siri, and sales-region options for activation attempts on China-mainland devices | | Advanced | Apple internal feature flags, the system-wide InternalBuild flag with explicit enable confirmation, internal settings bundle, Security Research Device flag | | Field editor | Read, search, add, edit, and remove `CacheExtra` fields; local plist import/export; String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Data, Date, Array, and Dictionary values | | Changes | Automatic reading and manual re-read, staged before/after review, verified writes, per-preset restore | | Backups | Automatic initial backup before device editing, backup before every write, original-value records; open, export, restore, and delete | | Logs & respring | Actual exploit-stage logs and manual NeoSpring respring | Usually, changing the region code is enough to try enabling AI; there is no need to change Sales Region. Selecting United States for Region Code sets `RegionCode` to `LL` and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code. *If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.* Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added. Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. China-mainland devices can use the Apple Intelligence and region options to attempt activation; availability also depends on the model, OS version, and Apple services. ### Apple Intelligence, Face ID and dictation The [YumEdit 1.2.1 approach](https://github.com/H4CNPE/YumEdit/tree/v1.2.1) avoids spoofing the product, board and CPU. In Intelligence, **Apple Intelligence Capability** sets the generative-model flag to `1`, while the separate **Siri AI Mode** preset sets `SiriMode` to `2`. Neither changes hardware identity nor the device-specific On-Device Siri capability. These are experimental flags, not a guarantee of resource downloads or working Apple Intelligence. YumEdit later replaced this activation approach with an experimental two-stage workflow; GestaltX does not implement temporary hardware spoofing. If a previous hardware spoof broke Face ID or dictation, choose an original device backup in **Backups → Restore Hardware Identity**. Alternatively, import a verified original plist and use **Intelligence → Restore Hardware Identity**. Save or discard pending changes first. Recovery requires a verified same-device backup with the same `CacheData`, `CacheUUID` and cache version, whose product and board match the kernel-reported hardware. It restores only product, board, CPU and the original regulatory model number, preserving current AI, Siri, region and unrelated settings. Unlike YumEdit's region activation, recovery does not substitute a US regulatory model. Missing, incompatible or already-spoofed backups are rejected; original hardware values are never guessed. Recovery currently recognizes iPhone 11 through iPhone 15/15 Plus (including the second- and third-generation SE), checking the original CPU against the known chip for the physical product. Other products are rejected rather than guessing their chip. A backup is created before writing and the complete result is verified. **Fully restart the device, then test Face ID, dictation and Apple Intelligence.** This recovery addresses hardware-spoofing damage, not every possible Face ID fault; device-level behavior still requires testing on affected hardware. ## Compatibility Supports **iOS / iPadOS 27.x**. **iOS / iPadOS 26.x is not supported for on-device MobileGestalt access.** Powered by [worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query). SystemGroup access requires iOS 27; available features depend on the device and OS. Local plist editing is also supported. Signing requires a certificate and provisioning profile with at least one usable App Group. Sign the app and its embedded share extension with at least one **common App Group**, and keep the extension when re-signing. Both processes detect their actual signed App Groups at runtime. Distributed IPAs carry ad-hoc signatures with these entitlements embedded so SideStore and AltStore can detect them when re-signing; they are not signed with a developer certificate. ## Download Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX/releases/latest). Some users report incomplete downloads with Safari on iOS 27. If the file is reported as damaged or cannot be extracted, download it again; several attempts may be needed. Try another browser if it persists. The cause has not been confirmed. ## Import a plist In Files or another app, select a MobileGestalt plist, tap **Share**, and choose **GestaltX**. The share extension reads the supplied file and hands it to the app through the shared App Group. Return to GestaltX if it does not open automatically. The app checks a device-bound proof from a GestaltX export, or at least two unique identifiers obtained from this device, then asks you to confirm the import. Files that cannot be verified are rejected. Previously imported files are never used as the reference for device identity. Some original plists contain no unique device identifiers. Export a copy from GestaltX on this device first: its verification key stays in the device-only Keychain and is never included in the file. Shared files are checked at launch and on return to the foreground. Pending edits are preserved until you save or discard them. Confirmed imports open as local documents. **MG Control** supports adding, editing, renaming and deleting typed keys and values. Use **Restore Imported Plist** to restore a verified file to this device; restoration requires a matching system cache layout and an additional confirmation, backs up the current file, and verifies the write. Restart the device afterward. ## Language support GestaltX follows your iOS language settings, with English as the default and fallback. Persian includes right-to-left layout support. | Language | Locale | | --- | --- | | English | `en` | | 简体中文 — Simplified Chinese | `zh-Hans` | | 繁體中文（台灣）— Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) | `zh-Hant-TW` | | 繁體中文（香港）— Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong) | `zh-Hant-HK` | | Tiếng Việt — Vietnamese | `vi` | | Русский — Russian | `ru` | | فارسی — Persian | `fa` | | 한국어 — Korean | `ko` | | Español — Spanish | `es` | | 日本語 — Japanese | `ja` | | Türkçe — Turkish | `tr` | ## Credits - [forcequitOS / Taj C — worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query) - [neonmodder123](https://github.com/neonmodder123) - [skadz108](https://github.com/skadz108) - [rooootdev — NeoSpring](https://github.com/rooootdev/neospring) - [Nouvborne — Ketamine](https://github.com/Nouvborne/Ketamine) - [PoomSmart — MGKeys](https://github.com/PoomSmart/MGKeys) - [leminlimez — Nugget](https://github.com/leminlimez/Nugget) - [rooootdev — mond](https://github.com/rooootdev/mond) - [frs0n — GestaltEdit](https://github.com/frs0n/GestaltEdit) ## Disclaimer For security research and educational purposes only. Developed by [huamidev](https://github.com/huamidev). ## Features | Category | Presets and tools | | --- | --- | | Display | Dynamic Island capability and layout, Always-On Display, AOD Vibrancy, high-luminance AOD, AOD flipbook, HDR photo display, wallpaper parallax, Liquid Glass low-power rendering, experimental PWM and DisplayPort flags | | Device | Model name, boot/shutdown chime, charge limit, tap to wake, Camera Control settings, Action Button settings, Collision SOS, Audio Mix, Spatial FaceTime audio | | iPad | Apple Pencil settings, Stage Manager capability, iPad app compatibility | | Intelligence | Independent region-code options, Apple Intelligence capability flag, on-device Siri, Audio Intelligence, Personal Translator, Photos Clean Up, Handwriting Synthesis, always-listening Hey Siri, and sales-region options for activation attempts on China-mainland devices | | Advanced | Apple internal feature flags, the system-wide InternalBuild flag with explicit enable confirmation, internal settings bundle, Security Research Device flag | | Field editor | Read, search, add, edit, and remove `CacheExtra` fields; local plist import/export; String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Data, Date, Array, and Dictionary values | | Changes | Automatic reading and manual re-read, staged before/after review, verified writes, per-preset restore | | Backups | Automatic initial backup before device editing, backup before every write, original-value records; open, export, restore, and delete | | Logs & respring | Actual exploit-stage logs and manual NeoSpring respring | Usually, changing the region code is enough to try enabling AI; there is no need to change Sales Region. Selecting United States for Region Code sets `RegionCode` to `LL` and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code. *If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.* Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added. Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. China-mainland devices can use the Apple Intelligence and region options to attempt activation; availability also depends on the model, OS version, and Apple services. ### Apple Intelligence, Face ID and dictation The [YumEdit 1.2.1 approach](https://github.com/H4CNPE/YumEdit/tree/v1.2.1) avoids spoofing the product, board and CPU. In Intelligence, **Apple Intelligence Capability** sets the generative-model flag to `1`, while the separate **Siri AI Mode** preset sets `SiriMode` to `2`. Neither changes hardware identity nor the device-specific On-Device Siri capability. These are experimental flags, not a guarantee of resource downloads or working Apple Intelligence. YumEdit later replaced this activation approach with an experimental two-stage workflow; GestaltX does not implement temporary hardware spoofing. If a previous hardware spoof broke Face ID or dictation, choose an original device backup in **Backups → Restore Hardware Identity**. Alternatively, import a verified original plist and use **Intelligence → Restore Hardware Identity**. Save or discard pending changes first. Recovery requires a verified same-device backup with the same `CacheData`, `CacheUUID` and cache version, whose product and board match the kernel-reported hardware. It restores only product, board, CPU and the original regulatory model number, preserving current AI, Siri, region and unrelated settings. Unlike YumEdit's region activation, recovery does not substitute a US regulatory model. Missing, incompatible or already-spoofed backups are rejected; original hardware values are never guessed. Recovery currently recognizes iPhone 11 through iPhone 15/15 Plus (including the second- and third-generation SE), checking the original CPU against the known chip for the physical product. Other products are rejected rather than guessing their chip. A backup is created before writing and the complete result is verified. **Fully restart the device, then test Face ID, dictation and Apple Intelligence.** This recovery addresses hardware-spoofing damage, not every possible Face ID fault; device-level behavior still requires testing on affected hardware. ## Compatibility Supports **iOS / iPadOS 27.x**. **iOS / iPadOS 26.x is not supported for on-device MobileGestalt access.** Powered by [worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query). SystemGroup access requires iOS 27; available features depend on the device and OS. Local plist editing is also supported. Signing requires a certificate and provisioning profile with at least one usable App Group. Sign the app and its embedded share extension with at least one **common App Group**, and keep the extension when re-signing. Both processes detect their actual signed App Groups at runtime. Distributed IPAs carry ad-hoc signatures with these entitlements embedded so SideStore and AltStore can detect them when re-signing; they are not signed with a developer certificate. ## Download Download the IPA from [Releases](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX/releases/latest). Some users report incomplete downloads with Safari on iOS 27. If the file is reported as damaged or cannot be extracted, download it again; several attempts may be needed. Try another browser if it persists. The cause has not been confirmed. ## Import a plist In Files or another app, select a MobileGestalt plist, tap **Share**, and choose **GestaltX**. The share extension reads the supplied file and hands it to the app through the shared App Group. Return to GestaltX if it does not open automatically. The app checks a device-bound proof from a GestaltX export, or at least two unique identifiers obtained from this device, then asks you to confirm the import. Files that cannot be verified are rejected. Previously imported files are never used as the reference for device identity. Some original plists contain no unique device identifiers. Export a copy from GestaltX on this device first: its verification key stays in the device-only Keychain and is never included in the file. Shared files are checked at launch and on return to the foreground. Pending edits are preserved until you save or discard them. Confirmed imports open as local documents. **MG Control** supports adding, editing, renaming and deleting typed keys and values. Use **Restore Imported Plist** to restore a verified file to this device; restoration requires a matching system cache layout and an additional confirmation, backs up the current file, and verifies the write. Restart the device afterward. ## Language support GestaltX follows your iOS language settings, with English as the default and fallback. Persian includes right-to-left layout support. | Language | Locale | | --- | --- | | English | `en` | | 简体中文 — Simplified Chinese | `zh-Hans` | | 繁體中文（台灣）— Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) | `zh-Hant-TW` | | 繁體中文（香港）— Traditional Chinese (Hong Kong) | `zh-Hant-HK` | | Tiếng Việt — Vietnamese | `vi` | | Русский — Russian | `ru` | | فارسی — Persian | `fa` | | 한국어 — Korean | `ko` | | Español — Spanish | `es` | | 日本語 — Japanese | `ja` | | Türkçe — Turkish | `tr` | ## Credits - [forcequitOS / Taj C — worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query) - [neonmodder123](https://github.com/neonmodder123) - [skadz108](https://github.com/skadz108) - [rooootdev — NeoSpring](https://github.com/rooootdev/neospring) - [Nouvborne — Ketamine](https://github.com/Nouvborne/Ketamine) - [PoomSmart — MGKeys](https://github.com/PoomSmart/MGKeys) - [leminlimez — Nugget](https://github.com/leminlimez/Nugget) - [rooootdev — mond](https://github.com/rooootdev/mond) - [frs0n — GestaltEdit](https://github.com/frs0n/GestaltEdit) ## Disclaimer For security research and educational purposes only. Use only on devices you own or are authorized to manage. Back up your data before making changes. Modifying MobileGestalt may cause system instability or require a device restore. You are responsible for the changes you apply and the resulting risks. ## License [GNU GPL v3](LICENSE) · Copyright © 2026 huamidev. ## Star History

rust-anything

English · Türkçe · Українська · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Deutsch · Français · Русский · 日本語 · 한국어 · Azərbaycanca · Oʻzbekcha · Қазақша · Кыргызча · Türkmençe · Татарча · ئۇيغۇرچە · Português · Tiếng Việt

Rewrite your app in Rust, and prove it still behaves the same.
Point it at your app: it records what the original does, your coding agent writes the Rust one piece at a time,
and every piece is checked against that recording before it moves on. It doesn't translate code; it proves the rewrite.


Install · Releases · Claude Code plugin · MCP Registry · Real-world ports · FAQ
Languages · How it works · Whole apps · Sponsors · MIT
Made in Türkiye 🇹🇷 by erKam Yaman · ❤️ Sponsor me · Sponsored by CodeRabbit

New in 2.0: Prettier, ported to Rust. 19x faster · 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs fully in Rust · every run byte-identical


Prettier against its Rust port on 59 real files from ms, Fuse.js and json-server (Apple M4). Same output, byte for byte. How it was measured.

PHP and C#: record, replay and the front door today; unit ports come next.

Record
record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws. 		Port
bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust. 		Check
diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes. 		Lift
When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby, Java or Kotlin app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It is built on [napi-rs](https://github.com/napi-rs/napi-rs), [PyO3](https://github.com/PyO3/pyo3) and [wasm-bindgen](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen), which carry the calls between your language and Rust; rust-anything decides what to move and proves it matches. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Whole tools and servers, or only the slow part, one hot path at a time: | Real project, same output as the original | Original | With rust-anything | | --- | ---: | ---: | | [Prettier](docs/real-world.md#prettier) 3.6.2, 2,360 JS/TS files from the command line | 128.6 s | **6.9 s: 19x faster** | | Prettier, 6,305 Markdown files from the command line | 352 s | **22.5 s: 15.6x faster** | | [json-server](docs/real-world.md#json-server), a whole Node server: memory at idle | 74 MB | **3.5 MB**, one 5.3 MB binary | | json-server, from start to first response | 79 to 85 ms | **8 to 10 ms** | | [Fuse.js](docs/real-world.md#fusejs) search over 50,000 strings, per query | 91.2 ms | **2.8 ms: 32x faster** | Prettier: 15,837 of 17,224 recorded runs format fully in Rust across 10 languages (JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, JSON, GraphQL, YAML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, Less), and all 17,224 match Prettier byte for byte, since anything not ported yet falls back to Prettier. json-server: 514/514 recorded HTTP cases match on a pure Rust binary. Measured on an Apple M4, two runs each, every output compared before timing ([details](docs/real-world.md)). Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. Against C the win is safety, not speed: [ffmpeg's libavutil](docs/real-world.md#ffmpeg) ported to Rust matches all 226,447 recorded calls and runs at about C's speed (18 of 42 benchmarks even, 8 faster, 16 slower by 3 to 40%).


json-server, a whole Node server, lifted to a pure Rust binary (Apple M4). How it was measured.

> rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project > or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation. > [!WARNING] > `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on > many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay` > run the same cases again, on the port or the original. Code that writes files, talks to a > database or calls the network does that once per case. Run them on a copy of the project, with a > test database and no production credentials in the environment. ## Quick start Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI or OpenCode and let your agent install it: ```text Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`. Tell me when to restart you. ``` Or yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # from crates.io rust-anything setup # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode ``` No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary. In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above must be on your `PATH`): ```text /plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything ``` `setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it. Then ask your agent, for example: - *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."* - *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."* - *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."* - *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."* ### Works with | Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds | | --- | --- | | Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` | | Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` | | Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | OpenCode | MCP server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`mcp.servers`), skill in `~/.config/opencode/skills/` | | Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](docs/install.md#install)) | Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`); `--no-backup` skips the copy. To wire OpenCode up by hand, put the server in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (`command` is the whole argv) and copy [`skills/rust-anything/`](./skills/rust-anything) to `~/.config/opencode/skills/rust-anything/`: ```json { "mcp": { "servers": { "rust-anything": { "type": "local", "command": ["rust-anything", "mcp"] } } } } ``` Or run the steps yourself: ```sh rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs # what is hot, and who calls it rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text # write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then: rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs # every recorded case must match rust-anything fuzz rust/fuzzy-rs --time 60 --keep # fresh inputs: what the recording missed rust-anything bench rust/fuzzy-rs # faster? the verdict says rust-anything gate rust/fuzzy-rs # done means this passes ``` rust-anything does not translate code: your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, ...) or you write the Rust. rust-anything supplies what an agent cannot guess reliably: where the time goes, what to port first and in which order, a bridge so the rest of the code calls the Rust with its API unchanged, the exact behavior the port must match, a safe way to ship it, and a gate that says when a port is done. Same output is not enough. Record what the app sends too, and a rewrite that mails twice fails:


A real run of app record --effects and app replay. See Side effects.

## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | Kotlin | Gradle module of top-level functions and `@JvmStatic` methods | the Java bridge: typed JNI in Java wrapper classes calling the compiled Kotlin statics | a generated reflection driver, with the Kotlin sources compiled by `kotlinc` | | PHP | folder of functions and `public static` methods | coming next: PHP FFI over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | C# | folder of `public static` methods | coming next: P/Invoke over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); a Gradle module with `.kt` sources and no `.java` sources is Kotlin, mixed modules stay Java. `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java, Kotlin and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. For Android, `rust-anything build --profile android` builds the same JNI library with the NDK for `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a` and `x86_64` (or the `--abi` values you pass) and installs it into `/jniLibs//`; `--api` sets the API level (minimum 26, which the generated Java runtime needs). It finds the NDK from `ANDROID_NDK_HOME`/`ANDROID_NDK_ROOT` or the SDK, needs the Rust targets (`rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi x86_64-linux-android`), links 64-bit libraries with 16 KB page alignment, and checks that every JNI entry point is exported. Gradle looks in `src/main/jniLibs` by default, so pass `--jni-libs app/src/main/jniLibs` or add `/jniLibs` to `sourceSets.main.jniLibs.srcDirs`. `rust-anything record --profile android` runs the original Kotlin unit under ART on a connected device (adb), dexes the generated driver with `d8` from the SDK's build-tools, and pulls the results back as the same `cases.jsonl`; `diff --profile android` replays them against the `.so` built for the device's ABI. Both need `adb`, a device, `kotlinc`, an SDK with build-tools and a platform, and `--device ` when more than one device is connected. The profile covers logic units: Activity/Compose/XML UI, lifecycle and SDK-only classes stay in Kotlin, and each call crosses JNI, so prefer the generated batch wrappers for hot loops. On a host, `record` and `diff` keep using the desktop JVM. For PHP, `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. Porting its units into Rust through PHP's FFI is the next step ([issue #2](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/2)). C# works the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door; porting units through P/Invoke comes next. ## Learn more - [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): the loop, what `bridge` and `analyze` decide, hot paths, what it can't catch, what a real port takes, and keeping up with the original (`map`) - [Ship a port as a package](docs/packaging.md): maturin wheels and napi-rs per-platform npm packages, with the CI that builds them - [Port a whole app](docs/whole-apps.md): servers, CLIs and libraries, from the front door to `app lift` - [Examples and case studies](docs/examples.md): x18n, and real code in six languages - [Real-world ports](docs/real-world.md): json-server, Fuse.js, vercel/ms, with benchmarks - [Install, update and develop](docs/install.md): every install method, Windows, and building from source - [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Status](docs/STATUS.md) · [MCP tools](docs/tools.md) ## Sponsors

rust-anything is free and open source. If it helps your work, please consider sponsoring it.
Your support keeps development going.
